question.text: SEBI requires mutual fund AMCs to disclose the commission paid to distributors in which of the following formats?

answer.text: Only in the annual report of the AMC
Only in the SID of each scheme
On the websites of the mutual fund/AMC and submitted to AMFI, where qualifying distributors' commissions and expense data are disclosed
SEBI does not require commission disclosure to investors

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series V-A workbook (p128), data relating to qualifying distributors — including commissions paid and expenses — is disclosed on the websites of the mutual fund/AMC and submitted to AMFI. Page 127 additionally requires distributors to disclose to investors the commissions earned from similar competing schemes being recommended. The Trap: The CAS described on p171-p172 is a transaction-and-holding statement issued to investors; it is not the channel SEBI prescribes for the website/AMFI disclosure of qualifying distributors' commission and expense data. The claim that no disclosure is required is plainly inconsistent with p127-p128. Note: Two distinct disclosures operate in parallel — website/AMFI publication of qualifying distributor commissions and expenses (p128), and the distributor's own disclosure of competing-scheme commissions to the investor at the point of recommendation (p127).
